setup.title: Welcome to Wardarr

issues.wardarrSectionHint: Problems inside Wardarr, not in your services.
issues.heroCalm: Nothing critical. Have a look when you have time.

settings.title: Settings
settings.instancesIntro: Each service can be connected several times. Instances are grouped by product.
settings.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other sessions were signed out.

cleaner.title: Queue Cleaner
cleaner.subtitle: Removes stuck downloads step by step, and only for a good reason.
cleaner.noInstances: No instance with a queue yet
cleaner.noInstancesBody: Connect Sonarr, Radarr or another *arr app in the settings. The Queue Cleaner starts in dry run.
cleaner.dryRunHint: Dry run: the Queue Cleaner records what it would do, but changes nothing in your services. Check the preview and the history, then arm it.
cleaner.armedHint: Armed: the Queue Cleaner removes downloads and searches again according to its rules.
cleaner.armBody: From now on, Wardarr removes stuck downloads in this instance, blocklists bad releases and searches again. Switch off other queue cleaners for this instance first, so two tools do not act on the same download. You can go back to dry run at any time.
cleaner.emptyBody: Nothing is stuck. Wardarr keeps watching.
cleaner.blocklistHelp: The *arr app will not grab this release again.
cleaner.searchAgainHelp: Looks for another release right after the removal.
cleaner.removeNote: This happens right away, even in dry run, because you start it yourself.
cleaner.reviewIntro: Check where each file would go. Wardarr only imports the files you select, after you confirm.
cleaner.importStarted: The import has started. The download leaves the queue once the *arr app is done.
cleaner.previewNoRun: The preview is ready after the first run.
cleaner.previewDryRun: In dry run, it only records this.
cleaner.historyEmptyBody: Every strike, removal and search shows up here with its rule and reason.
cleaner.attemptsIntro: After {{count}} removals of bad downloads, Wardarr stops searching a title so your indexers are not used up. Hunting skips these titles too.
cleaner.attemptsEmpty: Every title still has attempts left
cleaner.orphansIntro: Downloads in your download clients that no connected *arr instance knows. Wardarr never deletes them on its own.
cleaner.deleteOrphanTitle: Delete this download from the client?
cleaner.deleteOrphanBody: Wardarr removes the job from {{client}}. Choose whether the downloaded files go too.

s.enabledHelp: Off: Wardarr does not evaluate the queue of this instance.
s.maxStrikesHelp: A download with a problem collects one strike per interval.
s.strikeIntervalHelp: A new strike comes at the earliest after this time.
s.waitForImportClickHelp: Blocked downloads with a clean import preview wait for you instead of collecting strikes.
s.failedHelp: Downloads the client reports as failed collect strikes.
s.slowHelp: Downloads below the minimum speed collect strikes.
s.attemptsHelp: Removals with a new search before Wardarr stops searching the title.
s.maxRemovalsHelp: A safety limit: more removals wait for the next run.
s.protectedTagsHelp: Downloads with one of these tags (comma separated) are never touched.
s.whitelistHelp: Titles or download ids containing one of these words (comma separated) are never touched.

hunting.title: Hunting
hunting.subtitle: Searches missing titles and upgrades at a calm pace.
hunting.noInstances: No instance that can search yet
hunting.noInstancesBody: Connect Sonarr, Radarr or another *arr app in the settings.
hunting.successDetail: {{found}} of {{finished}} searches found something, {{imported}} imported (30 days)
hunting.upNextEmptyBody: Titles appear here after the next run, with the reason Wardarr picked them.

s.apiCallsHelp: All calls of Hunting on this instance count.
s.pauseQueueHelp: Hunting waits while the queue is this full.
s.seasonPacksHelp: Several missing episodes of a season become one season search.

discover.emptySearch: Try a different spelling or a shorter title.
discover.seasonsHint: Pick seasons, or leave all empty to request every missing season.
discover.requestedBody: The request is on its way. You can follow it under Requests.
discover.noServer: No server for this kind of title is set up in the request manager.

requests.intro: Everything you requested and where it stands.
requests.introAdmin: Approve, decline, adjust and retry requests.
requests.emptyMineBody: Find something in Discover and request it.
requests.linksIntro: Every request runs as the matching user in the request manager, so its permissions, limits and auto-approval stay in charge. Wardarr matches users by name; pick a user by hand where the names differ.
requests.linkNone: Not linked. This person cannot request yet.
requests.linkNoneAdmin: Not linked. Requests run as the API key owner.

library.intro: What is in the library and what is being watched.

library.noPlaysBody: Wardarr records plays while it is running.

indexers.intro: How your indexers are doing and which apps depend on them.

indexers.testFailed: Test failed. Check the indexer in Prowlarr.
indexers.stranded_one: {{list}} has no working indexer left while this one fails.
indexers.stranded_other: {{list}} have no working indexer left while this one fails.

notifications.intro: Wardarr tells you about new problems, when they are fixed and when a request waits for approval. A problem that fixes itself within a minute stays quiet.
notifications.emptyBody: Add a channel such as ntfy, Discord or Telegram, and Wardarr reaches you when something needs you.

kindHint.webhook: JSON to any address, optionally signed.
kindHint.discord: A message in a Discord channel.
kindHint.ntfy: Push to your phone through ntfy.sh or your own server.
kindHint.gotify: Push through your own Gotify server.
kindHint.telegram: A message from your Telegram bot.
kindHint.email: A message through your mail server.

fieldHelp.topic: Pick a long, hard to guess topic on public servers.
fieldHelp.signingSecret: Wardarr signs each message with HMAC-SHA256 in the x-wardarr-signature header.
fieldHelp.chatId: The chat, group or channel the bot writes to.
fieldHelp.host: The host name of your mail server.
fieldHelp.port: Usually 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with TLS.
fieldHelp.to: Up to ten addresses, separated by commas.
fieldHelp.username: Leave empty if the server does not need a login.

notifications.requestsHelp: Requests made in Wardarr that need an admin.
